text:
Priya: Customer hit intermittent timeouts + 502s on /v1/generate over the last 30m. They say their app logs show nothing useful and they can't find a request/trace id to send.
kevin: ok — for escalation we need a single failing example plus how to reproduce. minimal ask below.
alex: dropping a short checklist we can paste to the customer.
Priya: yes please. keep it non-technical for their devs but include commands for engineers.
kevin: customer checklist (short):
• One exact UTC timestamp (to the second) when the error occurred
• A HAR export of the browser session (if this happened in web) or a curl that reproduces the failing call
• The SDK session id or session hash (if using our SDK) or the full request headers from their proxy
• A screenshot of the network tab or the raw response body
• If mobile: a short log snippet (logcat/console) around the time

Priya: copyable steps (paste to customer):

Hi — to help us trace this quickly please send: 
1) One failing example: the exact UTC timestamp (e.g. 2024-07-11T15:12:03Z) and a HAR or curl for the request. If you can run curl, use: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```
We only need the headers/response — redact secrets before sending.

2) Look for a request header in your proxy or browser called `x-redwood-request-id` or `x-request-id`. If present, paste that value (looks like `req_3f2a4b1c`).

3) If you're using the Redwood JS/Android/iOS SDK, send the session id: run this in the page console (web):
```js
// run in browser console
console.log(window.__redwoodSession || window.RedwoodSession || 'not-found')
```
On Android native, paste the small log where you see `session=` or `session_hash`. For iOS look for `RedwoodSession` in the console.

4) If you can't get a request id, please export a HAR (chrome devtools -> Network -> right click -> Save all as HAR) covering the failure time and attach it.

5) (Optional) If the above is hard, enable a short debug token from your side and share it: run the SDK debug helper or paste the debug-token created from the Console (Support can walk you through this).

Notes for engineers: 
• To reproduce locally, capture a curl with verbose headers: `curl -v` and paste the `X-Redwood-Request-Id` header from the response if present.
• From a proxy (nginx/edge) logs, grep the request id: `grep -E "redwood|req_id|x-request-id" /var/log/nginx/access.log` and include the matching line.
• From mobile ADB: `adb logcat | grep -i redwood` (look for `req` or `session`).

alex: also add a short example of what we need to see in the HAR (request/response headers + response body).
kevin: yeah include that: we need the response status, response body (even if empty), and any header named `x-redwood-*` or `x-request-id`.

Priya: final customer message template (one-liner):
"Hi — we hit an intermittent 502/timeouts. Can you share: UTC timestamp, a HAR or curl reproducer, any `x-redwood-request-id` or `x-request-id` you see, and your SDK session id? Thank you!"

kevin: if they send a req id we can look it up in Console -> Requests -> filter by time -> paste id into search. copy the full trace and escalate to eng-runtime with the trace id and timestamp.

Priya: escalation checklist for eng: 
• req id (required)
• customer timestamp and sample client IP
• HAR/curl or SDK logs
• Whether they saw retries/bursts around that time

alex: one last tip — if customer can't collect a HAR because this happens server-side behind a proxy, ask for a 60s pcap or proxy access logs around timestamp.

kevin: ok i'm pasting this into the support reply now. :thumbsup:
Priya: thanks — mark as high-priority if they report production impact.
